rules.surface_condition: cuts that split a numeral token from an immediately following measurement/unit token (e.g., 1.2 <SEG> million, 240 <SEG> kilometers, 9,000 <SEG> year, 46 <SEG> percent, 378 <SEG> meters)
rules.blamed_rule: - Is the token immediately before the marker a numeral/date/percentage/name? If yes, bias score upward.
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring Rule: if the token immediately before the marker is NUM and the token immediately after the marker is a measurement/unit word, reduce the predicted value (move the marker out of the extreme-top ranks). Target band: lower scores into the mid–low band (recommend roughly 30–55) instead of boosting toward the top. Rationale: many such splits are low because splitting number from its scale/unit badly harms adequacy or is contradicted by the continuation.

rules.surface_condition: markers immediately followed by a clause-continuing subordinating token (right-first ∈ {because, due, causing, that, which, who, when, while, as})
rules.blamed_rule: - Is the token immediately after the marker a determiner/preposition/auxiliary/relative pronoun? If yes, bias score downward.
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring Rule: if the token immediately after the marker is a clause-continuing/subordinating word from the list (because, due, causing, that, which, who, when, while, as), apply a stronger downward adjustment than the generic 'preposition/determiner' bias — aim for a low band (recommend roughly 10–40) unless the opposite side contains a clear numeral/unit or an independent named entity that justifies a higher score. Rationale: these tokens often indicate the remainder will modify/overturn the left stretch and produce high contradiction measurements.

rules.surface_condition: markers immediately after short identifier/parenthetical-like tokens (short IDs and acronyms) such as parenthood, isil, kv62, minae, service
rules.blamed_rule: - Left or right stretch that ends or begins with a lexical token translators typically render reliably will tend to raise the measured value. Examples of such surface forms: numerals and formatted numbers (e.g., "1,200", "2050"), explicit dates, percentages, currency figures, and short fixed named phrases (e.g., organization names, place names). (Prediction to test: cuts adjacent to numerals/dates often score high.)
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring Rule: if the token immediately before the marker is a short identifier from the listed small-ID vocabulary (examples: parenthood, isil, kv62, minae, service), reduce the predicted value moderately (target band ~15–45), unless the token immediately after the marker is NUM or a clear measurement/unit/date (in which case do not apply this reduction). Rationale: short IDs are often part of a larger identifier or are followed by disambiguating material; cutting immediately after them commonly yields fragments or contradictions in the measured procedure.

summary: The model over-ranks cuts that split numerals from their unit words, that are immediately followed by clause-continuing subordinators (because/due/causing/that/which/...), and that occur right after short identifier/acronym tokens. These surface patterns recur across cases and correspond to high measured contradiction or fragment scores; moving them down (moderately, not brutally) should reorder boundaries so the deterministic keeper prefers safer cuts. Avoid the earlier hard, blanket demotions — prefer targeted, mid-strength downward shifts and one small exception to preserve genuinely good numeral-adjacent boundaries.
